description: In the post-classical Mediterranean world, Greek was essential for conveying and preserving the
religious stories, traditions, and beliefs of Jewish and Early Christian communities. Students in
this course expand their knowledge of ancient Greek language and literature by translating
selections from biblical texts including the Septuagint (Greek translation of Hebrew scriptures)
and the New Testament. Topics such as the origin of the universe, the nature of human suffering,
and conceptions of the divine are explored. Offered alternate years in the spring semester.
